liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **He's Gone** (5 reviews): Reviewer, who attended, found the haunting jam after He's Gone unique and slightly similar to a Dead jam style; Reviewer calls the He's Gone and the jam that follows incredible; also praises Saint of Circumstance [11][12][17][19][20]
- **Jam** (2 reviews): Jam after He's Gone made the arena feel like a small smoky bar somewhere in the Bowery; Both jams are on fire; the later one has very high energy, with notable Jerry and Bruce interplay [13][16]
- **Drums** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer says the beam came alive during drums; Uploader lists a second Jam between Drums and All Along The Watchtower [2][21]
- **Foolish Heart** (1 review): Reviewer says the band rocks out on Foolish Heart, possibly the hottest version on record [16]
- **Saint Of Circumstance** (1 other source): Taper stopped the deck mid-song, so his master lacks about two minutes of Saint [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd90-12-28SBDd1t01**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd90-12-28SBDd1t02**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd90-12-28SBDd1t03**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd90-12-28SBDd1t04**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd90-12-28SBDd1t05**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd90-12-28SBDd1t06**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd90-12-28SBDd1t07**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]
- **gd90-12-28SBDd2t01**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]

## The recordings

- **gd90-12-28.sbd-matrix.wiley.11498.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 161 min; rated 4.36/5 by 14 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording quality is good and gives the feeling of being present at the show; Bob's voice is strong; Described as a Healy Ultra Mix soundboard that sounds perfect [10][20]
- **gd1990-12-28.168850.nakcm300.cp4.ont.flac1644**: source not stated; 17 songs; 165 min [8]
- **gd1990-12-28.s1.127432.nak300.bowen.flac16**: source not stated; 7 songs; 64 min [9]
- **gd1990-12-28.136762.dusio.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 157 min [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended; says it was their second show with Hornsby, who played well, with grand piano backing the band [10]
- Reviewer gives the setlist: first set ends Victim into Foolish Heart; second set runs China Cat through Around, encore Black Muddy River [14]
- Reviewer recalls rain pouring when the show ended [21]
- Taper's second-set master was ruined by mushroom ingestion, trouble starting near the beginning of China Cat Sunflower [8]
- Part of a four-night run in which each night seemed better than the previous one [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd90-12-28.sbd-matrix.wiley.11498.sbeok.shnf**: source: (Healy Mix)SBD>??>DAT>CDR [1]
- **gd1990-12-28.168850.nakcm300.cp4.ont.flac1644**: taped by OldNeumanntapr; transferred by OldNeumanntapr; source: Set 1: Nakamichi CM 300x3; Two CP 4 Shotguns + 1 CP 1 Cardioid >Boss BX4 Mixer >Sony WM-D6C [MX 90] Set 2: Nakamichi CM 300 CP4 Shotguns >Sony TC-153SD [XLIIS… [8]. Also: Taped on newly bought, secondhand Nakamichi CM 300s, with a different microphone setup tried for each set [8]
- **gd1990-12-28.s1.127432.nak300.bowen.flac16**: taped by Jeff Bowen; transferred by Jeff Bowen; source: Source: Nakamichi CM-300x3; Two CP-4 Shotguns + One CP-1 Cardioid > Boss BX-4 Mixer > Sony WM-D6C (MX-S 90) [9]. Also: Nakamichi 300 recording from an OTS location; only Set I is circulated [9]
- **gd1990-12-28.136762.dusio.flac16**: taped by Chris Dusio; transferred by Chris Dusio; source: flac16: Recorded by Chris DusioAT835's>SonyD6>That's Metal Cassette>ZoomF8>Audacity [2]
